question.text: This economic and social campaign beginning in 1958 sought to rapidly transform China from an agrarian economy to modern communist society. It failed miserably.
question.clue: Millions of people were encouraged to set up backyard furnaces during this campaign.

swap.leadin: During this rebellion, a Muslim group called the Hansu Braves set fire to Hanlin Academy during the Siege of the Foreign Legations.
swap.text: Name this rebellion which occurred during the Qing [Ching] dynasty and was defeated by the Eight-Nation Alliance.
swap.answerHtml: Boxer Rebellion [or Boxer Uprising; or other synonyms for “rebellion;” or Yihetuan Movement]
swap.clue: The Open Door policy was formulated in response to this event, which was ended by the Eight-Nation Alliance and sparked by anger towards the unequal treaties.

question.leadin: A protest here led to Jeff Widener's iconic photograph of a man, possibly named Wang Weilin, standing in front of four tanks.
question.text: Name this Beijing square tragically cleared on the night of June 4, 1989 after Deng Xiaoping's conservative faction used their control of the military.
question.clue: In 1976, mass public displays of mourning at this site prompted disciplinary actions initiated by the Gang of Four.

swap.text: The UK turned over control of this Special Administrative Region to China in 1997, two years beforePortugal did the same with nearby Macau.
swap.clue: At that time, this polity was restored to its previous owner, who had this polity ceded to them in 1842 after the First Opium War.

question.text: The treaty ending the First Opium War was signed in this city. It was later the capital of the Kuomintang regime before and after the Second Sino-Japanese War.
question.clue: This city surrendered to the Manchu without a siege during the Fall of the Ming Dynasty, and one treaty named for this city was signed aboard the HMS Cornwallis, and ended the Thirteen Factories system.

swap.leadin: This man was given his new surname by the Yongle emperor.
swap.text: Name this Muslim eunuch who was comissioned to go on seven "treasure voyages" in the oceans south of China, ranging all the way to Africa. His ships were the largest wooden ships ever built.
swap.clue: This diplomat was given a giraffe and a zebra while taking tribute from Malindi and the Swahili coast.

question.leadin: Sir Halliday Macartney held this man hostage in a London embassy, which he described in the memoir Kidnapped in London.
question.text: Name this man who led the Xinhai revolution that toppled the Qing dynasty. This man served as the provisional first president of the Republic of China.
question.clue: His party's ideals were expressed in works like the Five-Yuan Constitution and the Three Principles of the People.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about a Chinese dynasty.
swap.text: The Tang golden age was brought to an end by this rebellion named for its leader, an ex-Tang general, who established the rival Yan Dynasty with his lieutenant Shi Siming. It was one of the costliest wars in human history.
swap.clue: This event began with the siege of Luoyang, and later saw the capture of the capital, Chang'an.

question.text: Article 1 recognized the autonomy of Korea, Article 2 ceded Formosa, and Article 4 stipulated an indemnity of two hundred million Kuping taels. For 15 points-such were the terms of what 1895 treaty ending the Sino-Japanese War?
question.clue: By this agreement, one side surrendered the Pescadores Islands, but a more controversial cession under it led to the so-called Triple Intervention.

swap.leadin: These people, under Yelu Dashi, moved to Central Asia and formed an eponymous "Kara Khanate."
swap.text: Name these people, originally from Manchuria, who began that khanate after defeating the Karakhanids and capturing Balasagun. These people's name is the origin of the historic name "Cathay" for China.
swap.clue: They divided their holdings into the Northern and Southern Chancellories and their emperors included men such as Shengzong and Jingzong, while their first ruler took the name Taizu and was known as Abaoji.

question.text: The Nihon Shoki attributes the introduction of Chinese characters to Japan to a state in a Korean period with this name. Cao Cao's exploits are featured in a Chinese novel named for this period.
question.answerHtml: Three Kingdoms [accept Three Kingdoms of Korea or Samhan of Korea; accept Sānguó Shídài; accept Romance of the Three Kingdoms or Sānguó Yanyì]
question.clue: In the lead up to this period, one side lost the Battle of Red Cliffs.

swap.text: This beloved consort of Tang Emperor Xuanzong, one of China's Four Beauties, was strangled by the emperor's attendant after his guards insisted she be killed. The guards blamed An Lushan's rebellion on her family.
swap.clue: This character sends that priest back to her lover with an inlaid box and a broken hairpin.

question.leadin: They're not explorers, but Zheng He was a famous Ming dynasty example of one of these men.
question.text: Give this general term that describes many servants of the Chinese imperial court. This type of male servant is castrated.
question.clue: In the Ottoman court, they were divided into black and white groups, with the chief black one controlling access to the Sultan, and in Assyria they included the rab-sa-resi (rab-sha-re-shi).

swap.leadin: This state gained power thanks to Shang Yang's reforms, and the kingdom of Han instantly surrendered to this kingdom when King An believed they would invade.
swap.text: Name this kingdom whose leader Ying Zheng conquered six other states, which began a namesake dynasty.
swap.clue: Li Si advised this dynasty's most notable ruler, who eventually died due to mercury poisoning while trying to find the elixir of life.

question.text: Chu's Pei County was the birthplace of this man, who struggled with Xiang Yu after Xiang inflicted several defeats on Qin forces. This man, who supposedly bore resemblance to a dragon, defeated Xiang Yu at the battle of Gaixia and founded a new line of rulers.
question.clue: Late in life, he favored Lady Qi as concubine, though she was murdered by his Empress afer his death.

swap.text: Amidst widespread instability and collapse of the monetary system, the Yuan ("ywen") dynasty was overthrown by these rebellions, an offshoot of the White Lotus movement.
swap.answerHtml: Red Turban rebellions [or Hóngjīn Qǐyì; accept answers with synonyms for “rebellion”]

question.leadin: This building was heavily looted in 1959 after thousands of protestors gathered in front of it during Women's Uprising Day.
question.text: The white section of what building, the Potrang Karpo, became a seat of government in 1649? The red section, the Potrang Marpo, was added in the 1690s.

swap.leadin: In 1058, this official submitted the Ten Thousand Word Memorial to Emperor Rensong, which foreshadowed the policies he later implemented under the "New Laws."
swap.text: Name this awesome 11th-century minister whose policies, including monetary expansion, progressive taxation, and old-age pensions, were ultimately scrapped by the conservative faction under his rival Sima Guang (SIH-mah GWAHNG).
swap.clue: This man created a financial bureau that raised officials' salaries while cutting the budget, instituted a 2-percent lending program for farmers through his "New Laws," and reformed the training of bureaucrats at the Hanlin Academy.

question.text: Until its capture by the Jurchens in 1127, the Song kept its capital in this city notable for the "Iron" Pagoda constructed in 1049, and for its Jewish community.
question.clue: The scroll painting Along the River During the Qingming Festival likely depicts the splendor of this capital city before its final two emperors, Qinzong ("cheen-dzong") and Huizong ("hway-dzong"), were captured in the Jingkang Incident.

swap.text: Peaceful "wo lei fei" in Hong Kong often participate in protests by performing this action. A controversial law passed in June 2020 made it a crime to lodge "insults" when this action was taking place in Hong Kong.
swap.answerHtml: singing [accept answers like singing the official or unofficial national anthem; accept playing a national anthem]
swap.clue: The Baltic countries gained independence from the Soviet Union in a "revolution" named for this action. That revolution named for this action included the formation of a human chain across all three countries.
